findings.before: Request payload source_revision could be copied into a COMPLIANT receipt.
findings.fix: Caller source_revision is forbidden. Runtime revision is resolved from process metadata; in GitHub Actions GITHUB_SHA is authoritative and a conflicting JANUS_SOURCE_REVISION fails closed.
findings.risk: An untrusted caller could choose the provenance string even though receipt_sha256 remained internally consistent.
findings.verification: Adversarial caller-override tests PASS on hardened main.

findings.before: Face-local verification did not uniformly enforce the exact receipt shape and every policy field.
findings.fix: Exact key set, identity, role, repository, runtime surface, capability scope, authority_weight, all acceptance booleans, enforcement scope, compliance state, source revision and checksum are verified.
findings.risk: A modified receipt could be re-hashed and accepted locally while Genesis rejected it.
findings.verification: Re-hashed policy/capability/release-control/extra-field tamper tests PASS by rejection.

findings.before: Bundle verification derived required_faces from the bundle under verification.
findings.fix: Genesis v1 owns CANONICAL_REQUIRED_FACES and rejects missing, extra, duplicate, unknown or reduced required Face sets.
findings.risk: A re-hashed internally consistent subset bundle could shrink its own required quorum.
findings.verification: Re-hashed quorum-downgrade adversarial test PASS by rejection.

findings.before: Source revisions were not uniformly restricted to commit-shaped hex identifiers or bound against an external expected revision map.
findings.fix: 40/64 hex revision validation plus exact expected_source_revisions binding during hardened four-Face replay.
findings.risk: A self-consistent receipt could identify an arbitrary non-empty revision.
findings.verification: Fresh post-merge v1.1 replay PASS with exact hardened main revisions.

findings.before: The receipt chain could be read too strongly if SHA-256 content addressing were interpreted as author authentication.
findings.fix: Canonical bundle and replay certificate explicitly encode SHA256_CONTENT_ADDRESS_NOT_SIGNATURE and external provenance requirements.
findings.risk: Checksum integrity could be confused with digital signature/origin attestation.
findings.verification: Hardened bundle requires these semantic fields and rejects re-hashed attempts to claim end-to-end authentication.

findings.before: Four independent Face receipts could be mistaken for a fully authenticated end-to-end message chain or unique process boot attestation.
findings.fix: Boundaries now distinguish invocation receipts, payload replay, cross-repo origin attestation, end-to-end message authentication and live deployment.
findings.risk: Independent invocation evidence is stronger than declarative configuration but weaker than chained process/message attestation.

remaining_open_gates.detail: Collect fresh receipts from actual NAS/production Face processes. GitHub CI remains non-production evidence.
If chain-level proof is desired, carry/verifiably bind upstream Face receipts or signed message attestations through DemiHead into Genesis.
If author/process origin must be cryptographically authenticated, adopt signed attestations or another trust-rooted provenance mechanism; SHA-256 alone is insufficient.

Current contract digest hashes symbolic reference strings, not the changing contents of referenced foundation/Armor artifacts. Add a versioned exact dependency manifest if transitive constitutional pinning is required.
Current implementation asserts the contract at module startup and emits a receipt per Face invocation; do not describe it as remote proof of one unique process boot.
